links.outcome: Expert-rated correctness, professionalism, completeness of KG-grounded RAG answers versus LLM-only
links.effect: Hybrid KG+LLM scored correctness 5.00, professionalism 5.00, completeness 4.40 versus LLM-only 4.05, 3.65, 4.12; all pairwise comparisons p<0.01.
links.quote: Across 60 evaluation questions, the KG ± LLM hybrid model achieved the highest mean scores on all three dimensions (correctness: 5.00; professionalism: 5.00; completeness: 4.40), significantly outperforming both the KG ± LLM template model (4.75, 4.77, 4.03) and the LLM-only model (4.05, 3.65, 4.12; all pairwise comparisons p < 0.01).

links.outcome: Traceability to source literature and distinguishing graph-derived from general-knowledge content
links.effect: Both KG-enhanced systems produced answers fully traceable to source literature across all 60 questions with no fabricated claims detected; experts valued layered presentation of high-confidence versus supplementary content.
links.quote: Notably, the hybrid model resolved the completeness limitation observed in the template-based approach, while both KG-enhanced systems produced answers fully traceable to source literature across all 60 questions, with no fabricated claims detected by expert reviewers.

unlisted_practices: Knowledge graph construction from literature to ground LLM answers in acupuncture (TCM) domain
Tiered confidence presentation separating graph-derived content from supplementary general knowledge

screen.reason: The study evaluates adding knowledge-graph retrieval grounding (RAG) to an existing LLM versus the ungrounded LLM-only model on clinical QA accuracy, hallucination prevention, and traceability evaluated by clinical experts.

primary.practice: retrieval grounding added to an existing tool
